quote: Example 1. Let X1, X2 be independent random variables such that Xi ∼ W − Exp(αi, β, γi), i = 1, 2. Also let Y1, Y2 be another pair of independent random variable such that Yi ∼ W − Exp(αi*, β, γi*), i = 1, 2 (the baseline distribution is Exponential with cdf, F(x) = 1 − e^{−γx}). The parameters are given in the form of matrices as [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] = [[4.8, 3.4],[2.5, 1.6]] ∈ P2 and [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] = [[4.03, 4.17],[2.005, 2.095]]. It can be observed that [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] = [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] T^{0.45}, and it satisfies the condition [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] ≺≺ [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] ⟹ X1:2 ≥hr Y1:2. The plot of the difference rY1:2 − rX1:2 is given in Figure 1 for β = 3.
